clue.text: Table arrangement for slimmer starting on diet?

indicators.note: starting picks out only the opening letter of the word slimmer

parts.note: a diet is an eating plan, a regime of what to eat

explanation.surface: A dieter asks whether someone slimming needs a special arrangement of their meals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' simply links the first letter to the rest; the question mark admits that 'diet' stands in loosely for the planned eating.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan showing where each guest sits is the usual arrangement of people around a dinner table.

clue.text: Spain guarantees recreation for elderly people

indicators.note: recreation read as re-creation, making these letters anew in a different order

explanation.surface: Spain promises leisure activities for its pensioners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recreation' looks like leisure for the old, but read as re-creation it rearranges SPAIN plus GUARANTEES.
explanation.definitionFit: People in their seventies are a particular group of the elderly, named from the Latin for seventy.

clue.text: Astray on the ocean

definitions.meaning: astray here means confused, lost, not knowing what to do
literally sailing, out on the open water

explanation.definitionFit: Being all at sea means bewildered, while the literal phrase means out on the water in a ship.

clue.text: Battle I almost won with James the First?

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: Jim is a familiar short form of the name James
A is first, as in the top grade or A1

explanation.surface: Someone boasts that they nearly won a battle alongside King James I.
explanation.walkthrough: 'James the First' looks like the Stuart king, but splits into JIM and A, the first letter or grade.
explanation.definitionFit: Iwo Jima was the island fought over by US and Japanese forces in 1945, a famous Pacific battle.

clue.text: Where teams play for sufficient reasons

definitions.meaning: sports fields or stadiums where matches are held
justification, as in good cause for a complaint

explanation.definitionFit: A football club plays at its home pitch, and a reason that justifies action is a basis in law or argument.

clue.text: Local leader, European or African

indicators.note: leader picks out the front letter of the word Local

parts.note: an Iberian is someone from Spain or Portugal, so a European

explanation.surface: A town official might be European or from Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local leader' looks like a council head, but just supplies the first letter, L.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of Liberia, a West African republic, is an African by nationality.

clue.text: Paris can do deals to develop a French region

indicators.note: to develop means these letters grow into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: The capital can negotiate deals to build up one of France's provinces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to develop' looks like regional planning for the capital, but it is the signal to rearrange all four words.
explanation.definitionFit: Nord-Pas-de-Calais was an administrative area of northern France, bordering the Channel and Belgium.

clue.text: Annoyed, having come to a climax, so to speak

indicators.note: so to speak signals that the words are said aloud and sound like another word

parts.note: having reached the top or high point means peaked

explanation.surface: Someone is irritated after things reach their climax, as one might say.
explanation.definitionFit: To be piqued is to feel irritated or resentful because one's pride has been hurt.

clue.text: A Japanese entertainer — she gets involved with a GI

indicators.note: gets involved suggests the letters becoming tangled together in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the letters of A and GI

explanation.surface: A Japanese hostess becomes romantically involved with an American soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets involved with' reads as romance but scrambles SHE with A GI.
explanation.definitionFit: Geishas are traditional Japanese women trained to entertain guests with music, dance and conversation.

clue.text: One has little time to cover history of painting technique

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: to cover means one piece is wrapped around the other

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a short space of time
the past is history, what has gone before

explanation.surface: Someone short of time summarises the history of a painting method.
explanation.walkthrough: 'history' reads as the history of art, but simply means what has gone before; 'has' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Impasto is the technique of laying on paint so thickly that brush or knife marks stand out.

clue.text: A dramatist carried on like this, looking back

indicators.note: on means the second piece follows on after the first
looking back means the little word is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: so means in this way or like this
borne is the past participle of bear, meaning carried

explanation.surface: A playwright continued in this vein while looking back at his past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carried on' looks like a phrase meaning continued; split it, with 'on' placing the turned SO first.
explanation.definitionFit: John Osborne was the English playwright behind Look Back in Anger, a hint the clue plays on.

clue.text: No one cheers — pop singer retreats, howling

indicators.note: retreats means the whole sequence goes backwards, read from the end

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
ta is British slang for thanks, like cheers
Lulu is a Scottish pop singer famous since the 1960s

explanation.surface: Nobody applauds as a pop star withdraws from the stage wailing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreats' turns the whole run around, not just the singer; 'No one' looks like nobody but splits in two.
explanation.definitionFit: Ululation is a long wavering howl or wail, as of grief or celebration.

clue.text: Binders known by old hands

definitions.meaning: things used for tying or binding, lengths of cord
experienced people are said to know the procedures of a job, from the sailing idiom

explanation.definitionFit: Cords bind things together, and veterans who know how things work are said to know them.

clue.text: Follow eastern bigwig in Venice

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them closely

explanation.surface: Tail an important Eastern figure in Venice.
explanation.definitionFit: The Doge was the elected chief magistrate who ruled the old Venetian republic.

clue.text: Order a lot of water for Old Nick?

parts.note: to marshal is to arrange or put in order
a sea is a large body of water

explanation.surface: Someone orders a great deal of water for the Devil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old Nick' looks like the Devil, but 'nick' is British slang for a prison, so an old prison.
explanation.definitionFit: The Marshalsea was a notorious historic debtors' prison in Southwark, London, so an old jail.

clue.text: Worker from the outskirts of Prague interrupting speaker

indicators.note: interrupting means the pair breaks into the middle of the other word

parts.note: an orator is a public speaker

indicators.note: the outskirts of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A worker from the suburbs of Prague heckles a speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: P and E, the ends of Prague, go into ORATOR after its O.
explanation.definitionFit: An operator is someone who works a machine or service, such as a telephone operator.

clue.text: Family doctor warns about seafood

parts.note: kin are one's family or relatives
GP is a general practitioner, a family doctor in Britain

indicators.note: about means the letters are turned around into a different order

explanation.surface: A family doctor warns patients about eating shellfish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Family doctor' looks like a single medic, but the two words give separate pieces; 'about' rearranges the warning, leaving RAWNS.
explanation.definitionFit: King prawns are a large variety of prawn, a type of shellfish eaten as seafood.

clue.text: One may be employed in zoo, dungeon and conference centre

definitions.text: One may be employed in zoo

parts.note: the keep is the strongest inner tower of a castle, home of the dungeon

indicators.note: centre picks out the middle two letters of the ten-letter word conference

explanation.surface: Someone might be hired to work at a zoo, a prison and a conference venue.
explanation.walkthrough: The list reads as three workplaces, but only 'zoo' belongs to the definition; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A zookeeper looks after the animals, so a keeper is someone a zoo employs.

clue.text: Careless freedom in desert

definitions.meaning: uninhibited lack of restraint, as in dancing with gay disregard
to leave someone behind and give up on them

explanation.definitionFit: To do something with wild unrestraint is to act with careless freedom, and to leave someone is to forsake them.

clue.text: Dinner — without noise, without wine — is less pleasant

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, the remaining letters go around the next piece
the first without means take away, removing the word from the meal

parts.note: a din is a loud noise
Asti is a sparkling Italian wine

explanation.surface: A dinner without noise or wine turns out to be rather less enjoyable.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'without' means minus, leaving NER; the second uses the old sense of outside, so NER goes round the wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Nastier is the comparative of nasty, meaning more unpleasant.

clue.text: A flower Theseus regularly picked?

indicators.note: regularly picked means every other letter is taken from the name

explanation.surface: Did the Greek hero Theseus routinely gather a bloom?
explanation.walkthrough: A 'flower' here is something that flows, a river; the Tees runs through north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: The River Tees flows through northern England, and a river is a crossword flower, being something that flows.

clue.text: Take up residence in a Yorkshire town

definitions.meaning: to make one's home somewhere permanently
A market town in North Yorkshire, in the Dales

explanation.definitionFit: To make one's home in a place is to put down roots there, and the word is also a North Yorkshire town name.

clue.text: Queen or rook captured? That may be a false move

indicators.note: captured means the chess piece is held inside the other letters

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
R is the chess abbreviation for rook

explanation.surface: A chess player asks whether a queen or rook was taken, which may have been a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess picture misleads: 'captured' puts the rook's letter inside the queen-plus-or run, not a piece taken off the board.
explanation.definitionFit: A mistake is something done wrongly, which a wrong move in a game is.

clue.text: Fool a long way off, missing the first or second?

parts.note: an ass is a foolish person

indicators.note: missing the first means the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: distant means far away

explanation.surface: A fool far away has missed out on coming first, or maybe second.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first or second' reads as a pair of placings, but 'or' links and 'second' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A second is a helper, as in a duel or boxing, someone who supports a principal.

clue.text: African belt has flipping external borders

indicators.note: flipping means the little word is turned over and read backwards
borders are the edges, here the first and last letters of the word external

explanation.surface: An African belt has flip-over outer edges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'belt' looks like a strap, but it is a geographical band.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sahel is the semi-arid band of land south of the Sahara stretching across Africa.

clue.text: A decent reform, as established by law

indicators.note: reform means the letters are formed again into a new order

explanation.surface: A decent reform has been passed by law.
explanation.definitionFit: A law is enacted when it is formally made into a statute, so established by legislation.

clue.text: Dreadful lies about Ham being outcast son of Abraham

indicators.note: dreadful suggests the words are mangled together into another arrangement

explanation.surface: Terrible lies are told about Ham, a biblical figure, in the story of Abraham's banished son.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of LIES and HAM are mixed as one pool; 'about' and 'being' only link. Ham is Noah's son, a decoy from the same book.
explanation.definitionFit: Ishmael was Abraham's son by Hagar, sent away into the wilderness in Genesis.

clue.text: What actuates Zebedee to get a car? The starter?

parts.note: Zebedee, from the British children's show The Magic Roundabout, bounces about on a spring
a Rolls is a Rolls-Royce car

explanation.surface: What sets the bouncing Zebedee going so he can get a car, and the engine starting?
explanation.walkthrough: Zebedee is a character from the British children's television show The Magic Roundabout who moves on a spring; 'starter' is a first course, not an engine starter.
explanation.definitionFit: Spring rolls are a common appetiser, so a dish served as a starter.
